full_judgment:
Kazi Md Ejarul Haque Akondo J: In this Rule Nisi, issued under article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents were called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 (decree signed on 4-8-2003) passed by the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra  (respondent No. 2) in Bankruptcy Case No. 03 of 2000 (Annexure-C) and the proceeding of Bankruptcy Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 (Annexure-J) now pending before the Bankruptcy Court No. 3, Bogra (respondent No.5) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 (Annexure-C) and the proceeding of Bankruptcy Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 (Annexure-J) were stayed for a period of 6 (six) months from date which was subsequently extended time to time. 

 5. On conclusion of trial, the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra, the respondent No. 2 by judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 decreed the suit on contest. Pursuant thereto, the decree-holder- bank, the respondent No.4 filed decree execution case being No. 02 of 2004 before the said Bankruptcy Court, which is now pending for disposal before the respondent No. 5, the Bankruptcy Court No. 3, Bogra (Annexure-J). 

 6. It has been stated that there is no provision of filing bankruptcy decree execution case in the Act-1997. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 and the proceeding of Bank-ruptcy Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 2004, the petitioners had filed this application and obtained the instant Rule. 

 8. The respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank limited, head office, Dhaka entered appearance and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter-alia, that the petitioners contested the suit in the trial Court and the suit was decreed on contest on 28-7-2003 against which they did not prefer appeal before the Hon'ble High Court Division as per provision of section 96 of the Act, 1997 as such, the instant writ petition is not maintainable in its present form. It has also been stated that after the said judgment and decree the respondent-bank tried to contact the petitioners for recovery of the decretal amount but they did not respond to the same as such, the respondent-bank lastly filed the execution case being Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 2004. It has further been stated that the petitioners are not aggrieved persons, their fundamental rights have not been infringed and their legal rights have not been violated as such, the writ petition is not maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 9. At the outset, Mr Md Helal Uddin Mollah, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Judge of the Bankruptcy Court passed the impugned judgment and decree without following the relevant provisions of the Act, 1997. He further goes to argue that the impugned decree execution case and its proceeding is barred by law, since there is no such provision to execute the judgment and decree of the Bankruptcy Court through instituting execution case. In the circumstances, he prays for disposing of the Rule in the light of the judgment passed in Writ Petition Nos. 7798 and 7799 of 2014. 

 10. Conversely, Mr Hironmay Halder, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.3 submits that as per the mandatory provision of section 96 of the Act, 1997 the petitioner is to file appeal against the impugned judgment and decree before the Hon'ble High Court Division by paying 10% of the decretal amount as such, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged for the ends of justice. 

 12. Admittedly, the impugned judgment and decree was passed by the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra and as per section 96 of the Act, 1997 any person aggrieved by a decision or an order made in the exercise of bankruptcy jurisdiction may prefer appeal before the High Court Division by paying 10% of the total value of the claim of creditors as determined by the Court. 

 "In view of the above well settled proposition of law as to the question of maintainability of the writ petition, we have no hesitation to hold that the petitioner has miserably failed to cross the first hurdle as to the question of maintainability of the instant writ petition mainly on two courts. Firstly, since the Bankruptcy Act is a special law and special provision having been provided in section 96 of the Bankruptcy Act, 1997 for preferring appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Bankruptcy Court and therefore, the question of entertaining an application under Article 102 of the Constitution does not arise at all. Secondly, whether notice/summons was properly served or not or whether the petitioner was a guarantor/mere a shareholder of the borrower company or borrowed money from the bank or not is disputed question of facts and for which remedy lies in the Civil Court and, not under summary writ jurisdiction. So, in order to save the valuable public time since the petitioner could not cross the first hurdle, we do not think it wise to advert to the lengthy arguments made by Mr Md Idrisur Rahman for the petitioner." 

 14. Moreover, in an unreported recent decision passed in Writ Petition Nos. 7798 and 7799 of 2014 this Division Bench (wherein one of us was a party) held that writ petition is not maintainable challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Bankruptcy Court. 

 16. In view of the above findings and decisions, we are of the opinion that the 1st portion of the instant Rule so far as it relates to the challenging of the impugned judgment and decree of the Bankruptcy Court is not maintainable in its present form. 

 17. Now, we are to see whether the 2nd portion of the instant Rule with respect to the institution of bankruptcy decree execution case pursuant to the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 and its continuation is maintainable in its present form or not? 

 18. In the case in hand, the decree-holder-bank pursuant to the impugned judgment and decree filed the impugned Bankruptcy Decree Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 before the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra, which was subsequently transferred to the Bankruptcy Court No. 3, Bogra, the respondent No.5 for disposal. 

 19. However, there is no such provision of filing execution case in the Act, 1997 to execute the judgment and decree of the Bankruptcy Court; rather there is a provision of appointing "Receiver" under section 64 of the said Act for recovery of the decretal amount from the judgment debtor. 

 20. In Writ Petition Nos. 7798 and 7799 of 2014 (as mentioned hereinbefore) this Bench declared the proceeding of bankruptcy decree execution case as without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect. 

 22. However, we are of the view that the decree-holder-respondent-bank may file application, if so advised, before the Bankruptcy Court concerned in respect of appointment of Receiver to execute the judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 (Annexure-C) and to recover the decretal amount from the judgment debtors and in that case, the Court concerned be at liberty to deal with the matter expeditiously preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment in accordance with law.
